title: Be the loop
intro: You are the counting loop. Before every pass you check the loop's condition: keep going while it is true, and stop the moment it is false.

rounds.prompt: Run the loop over `{name}`: check the condition, let the body run, then press `i++`.
rounds.right: `{length} < {length}` is false, so the loop ends. Every index from 0 to {last} was visited exactly once.

why.early: `{i} < {length}` is still true, so the loop isn't finished: stopping here would skip {missed}.
why.late: `{i} < {length}` is false. Run the body now and it reads `{name}[{i}]`, a box that doesn't exist: an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. A length-{length} array has indexes 0 to {last}.

rounds.prompt: The first {start} passes have run. Take over at `i = {start}` and finish the loop over `{name}`.
rounds.right: The loop stops at `i = {length}` without running the body, so it only ever reads indexes 0 to {last}: `<` keeps every read inside the array.

why.early: `{i} < {length}` is still true: the loop goes on, and stopping here would skip {missed}.
why.late: `{i} < {length}` is false. One more pass would read `{name}[{i}]`, one box past the end, and the program would crash with an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

rounds.right: `{name}[0]` is the first box and `{name}[{name}.length - 1]` the last: the indexes run from 0 to {last}.

why.click: That one is `{clicked}`. Indexes count from 0 at the first box, so `{expr}` is the box {index} steps along from the start.
why.last: That one is `{clicked}`. `{name}.length` is {length}, so `{name}.length - 1` is {last}: the last box, because the first one is index 0.
